Writing Tips for Writing in the Unreal Past
You can write about imagined events in the past by using the third conditional.
Conditional sentences show that one situation is dependent on another for that situation to happen.

If you want to talk about unreal events in the past, you can use the third conditional. You cannot change these events because they have already been done. You are just imagining how things could have been different.

How to form the third conditional:
if + past perfect, would have + past participle

In writing, it is especially important that you remember to use commas if the if-clause comes before the main clause.
If the condition clause (if-clause) comes after the main clause, there is no need to use commas.

If I won the lottery, I would buy my parents a house.
I would buy my parents a house if I won the lottery.

If I had studied harder, I would have passed the test the first time.
I would have passed the test the first time if I had studied harder.

Other expressions that refer to conditions are:
even if (meaning: “something would happen or would have happened no matter what”)
only if (meaning: “only on this one condition”)

Examples:
My sister is a terrible cook. I wouldn't eat the food she cooks even if I were starving.
Even if Diana had earned more money, she wouldn't have bought a handbag for $900. She had other reasons for not buying the handbag.

I would go to Bali only if I got a free ticket.
Only if I got a free ticket, would I go to Bali. 🌟
(The only way I would go to Bali was if I got a free ticket.)

Jorge would have bought a new TV only if his roommate had shared half the cost.
Only if his roommate had shared half the cost, would Jorge have bought a new TV. 🌟
(The only way Jorge would have bought a new TV was if his roommate had shared the cost.)
🌟 Notice that when only if begins a sentence, you need to invert the subject and verb in the main clause. 🌟
For example,  I would never show up late to work or leave early even if I wanted to.
If I had known what their true personalities were like when I hired them, I would have shown them the door on the first day.
If I hadn't decided to stop tearing my hair out and start making some major changes, I would have gone crazy.
Plus, if we had won the lotto, we would have done the exact same thing.

Write a 150-170 word personal e-mail to a family member (aunt, uncle, cousin, grandparent) that you haven't connected with in a long time.
Use a casual greeting and a friendly closing.
State why you are e-mailing.
Explain what you have been doing in the last two months.
Ask your family member two questions.
Express your feelings about being apart.
When completed, read your e-mail aloud to a partner.
I write a personal e-mail to a family member.
I ask questions in an e-mail.
I read my e-mail aloud to a partner.

(noun)
Example: Any drive quickly disappears.

Describing Character Traits
A character trait is a word or phrase that describes a person's personality and behavior.
Your creativity, positivity and dynamic nature always gave me some perspective.
You can use certain phrases to express character traits. You use these phrases with nouns, adjectives , adverbs and expressions.

Some phrases you can use are:
People behave + adverb (People behave so irresponsibly.)
You have a (adjective) nature (You have such a dynamic nature.)
I miss your + noun (I miss your creativity and positivity.)
They act (like) + noun, adjective, adverb (They act like children.)
I just can't understand how people can behave so unprofessionally in the workplace.
The remaining staff act like children who expect everything for nothing.
